blocks.text: Hadhrat Jareer bin Abdillaah (RA) Pledges to Listen, to obey and to Wish Well for all Muslims

Ibn Jareer narrates from Hadhrat Jareer (RA) that he pledged to listen, to obey and wish well for all Muslims. Ibn Jareer also reports another narration from Hadhrat Jareer (RA) in which he states that he approached Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "May I pledge at your hands that I shall listen and obey whether I am willing or unwilling?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "Do you have the ability to do this? Refrain from saying so and say rather that you will do so to the best of your ability." Hadhrat Jareer (RA) then added, "To the best of my ability." Rasulullaah ﷺ accepted the pledge together with the pledge to wish well for all Muslims.[^1]

Abu Dawood and Nasa'ee narrate from Hadhrat Jareer (RA) that he pledged to listen, to obey and wish well for all Muslims. Therefore, whenever Hadhrat Jareer (RA) bought or sold anything, he would say to the opposite person, "The thing I have taken from you is more beloved to me than that which I have given to you, so decide (whether you want to go ahead with the transaction or not)."[^2]
Hadhrat Utba bin Abd (RA) pledges allegiance and Rasulullaah ﷺ's Advice to Add the words "To the best of my Ability"
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that whenever the Sahabah (RA) pledged to listen and to obey at the hands of Rasulullaah ﷺ, he told them to add the clause: "To the best of my ability."[^3]
Hadhrat Utba bin Abd (RA) narrates that he pledged allegiance to Rasulullaah ﷺ seven times. On five occasions he pledged obedience and on two he pledged his love.[^4]
Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "With these very hands did I pledged allegiance to Rasulullaah ﷺ that I would listen and obey to the best of my ability."[^5]
